name: Open Privacy Programme Framework
summary: A sequenced, scalable implementation framework for data protection programmes. One control catalogue, three scaling profiles, four phases and a maturity model, mapped to eight data protection laws, ISO/IEC 27701 and the NIST Privacy Framework, with ISO/IEC 42001 and the EU AI Act for AI controls.

profiles.label: Essential
profiles.who: Small organisations with low-risk processing: the legal floor plus the habits that keep it true.

profiles.label: Standard
profiles.who: Mid-sized organisations, or any organisation with sensitive data or a regulator that audits: a managed, evidenced programme.

profiles.label: Advanced
profiles.who: Regulated sectors, very large volumes, groups and certification candidates: an assured, measured programme.

phases.name: Foundation
phases.goal: Mandate, ownership, knowing your data, and the legal must-haves that carry penalties on their own.

phases.name: Operate
phases.goal: Repeatable processes for assessments, rights, vendors, transfers, retention and incidents.

phases.name: Assure
phases.goal: Monitoring, testing, training in depth and internal audit, so the programme can prove it works.

phases.name: Optimise
phases.goal: Measurement, automation, certification and continual improvement.

domains.name: Governance and accountability
domains.purpose: Leadership commitment, ownership, policy and the ability to demonstrate compliance.

domains.name: Regulatory obligations
domains.purpose: Knowing which laws apply and meeting registration, filing, representative and regulator duties.

domains.name: Data inventory and records
domains.purpose: Knowing what personal data you hold, where, why and who touches it.

domains.name: Lawful and fair processing
domains.purpose: A documented legal basis for every purpose, with the extra conditions sensitive and children’s data need.

domains.name: Transparency
domains.purpose: Telling people what happens to their data, at the right moment and in plain language.

domains.name: Individual rights and complaints
domains.purpose: Receiving, verifying and answering requests and complaints within each law’s deadline.

domains.name: Risk, assessments and privacy by design
domains.purpose: Finding privacy risk early and treating it before processing starts.

domains.name: Third parties and transfers
domains.purpose: Choosing, contracting, overseeing and exiting vendors, and lawful transfers abroad.

domains.name: Security of processing
domains.purpose: Technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk.

domains.name: Data lifecycle
domains.purpose: Collecting only what is needed, keeping it accurate, and disposing of it on time.

domains.name: Incidents and breaches
domains.purpose: Detecting, assessing, notifying and learning from personal data breaches.

domains.name: People and culture
domains.purpose: Training, competence and the behaviours that make controls work.

domains.name: AI and automated decisions
domains.purpose: Governing AI systems and automated decisions that use personal data or affect people.

domains.name: Assurance and improvement
domains.purpose: Monitoring, audit, management review and continual improvement.

triggers.processor: Processes personal data for clients (acts as processor)
triggers.website: Runs public websites or apps that use cookies or similar technologies
triggers.sensitive: Processes sensitive or special category data
triggers.ai: Uses AI or makes automated decisions about people
triggers.transfers: Transfers personal data across borders, including to cloud services abroad
triggers.monitoring: Monitors people (CCTV, employee monitoring, location or biometric tracking)
triggers.representative: Needs a local representative (subject to GDPR or UK GDPR without an establishment there)
triggers.consent: Relies on consent for some processing

ISO27701.name: ISO/IEC 27701
ISO27701.note: Second edition, October 2025. Standalone privacy information management system; clauses 4–10 plus Annex A (A.1 controller, A.2 processor, A.3 shared controls). Clause numbers follow the harmonised structure; Annex A control numbers are not reproduced here.

NISTPF.name: NIST Privacy Framework
NISTPF.note: Version 1.0 (January 2020) is the only final version. Version 1.1 was an initial public draft in April 2025. Categories cited are from 1.0.

ISO42001.name: ISO/IEC 42001
ISO42001.note: AI management system. Cited by clause or Annex A topic.

EUAIA.name: EU AI Act
EUAIA.note: Cited for organisations placing or using AI systems in the EU market.

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.law: Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and General Application and Implementation Directive 2025

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.law: Protection of Personal Information Act 2013 (POPIA) and PAIA

KE.name: Kenya
KE.regulator: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner

EG.name: Egypt
EG.law: Personal Data Protection Law 151 of 2020 and Executive Regulations

UK.name: United Kingdom
UK.law: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018

controls.title: Executive mandate and programme charter
controls.objective: The board or executive has approved the programme’s scope, objectives, authority and reporting line, and the charter is reviewed each year.
steps: Brief the executive on the laws in scope, the penalties and the current exposure.
Agree scope: entities, jurisdictions, business units and systems.
Approve a one-page charter: objectives, authority, reporting line, budget owner.
Name an executive sponsor accountable for the programme.
deliverables: Board or executive minute approving it
controls.notes: Keep it short. A charter that runs to ten pages is rarely read again; one page signed by the CEO changes behaviour.

controls.title: Privacy lead appointed with independence and resources
controls.objective: A competent person is formally appointed as DPO, Information Officer or privacy lead, reports to senior management, is free from conflicts and is registered or notified where the law requires.
steps: Decide whether the law makes the appointment mandatory for each entity.
Appoint in writing, with a role description that covers the statutory tasks.
Check for conflicts of interest (for example the head of IT or marketing acting as DPO).
Publish the contact details and notify or register them with each regulator that requires it.

NG.note: Data controllers and processors of major importance.

ZA.note: The head of a private body is the Information Officer by default.

ZA.ref: Information Officer registration with the Information Regulator

KE.note: Appointment is optional in the Act but expected by the ODPC for larger controllers.

GH.note: Data Protection Supervisor. The pending Data Protection Bill 2025 would replace this with a DPO.

EG.ref: PDPL 151/2020 (DPO appointment and registration with the PDPC)

ZW.ref: CDPA 2021 s.20; SI 155 of 2024 (DPO notified to POTRAZ within 90 days)

EU.note: Where Art. 37(1) applies; otherwise good practice.

controls.title: Roles, responsibilities and privacy champions
controls.objective: Every function that touches personal data knows what it owns. A RACI covers the programme and each department has a named champion.
steps: List the programme activities in this framework that apply to you.
Assign responsible, accountable, consulted and informed roles for each.
Nominate a champion in each department that processes personal data.
Write the responsibilities into job descriptions where they are material.

controls.title: Data protection policy
controls.objective: A board-approved policy sets the organisation’s data protection commitments and points to the procedures that implement them.
steps: Draft the policy around the principles and the laws in scope; keep procedures separate.
Cover roles, lawful processing, rights, security, vendors, transfers, retention, breaches and training.
Approve at executive level and publish internally.
Set an annual review date.
evidence: Approved policy with version and date

NG.ref: GAID 2025 (data protection policy, reviewed in the Compliance Audit Return)

KE.ref: ODPC guidance note on data protection policies

controls.title: Management reporting and oversight
controls.objective: Management receives regular reports on privacy risk, incidents, requests and programme progress, and acts on them.
steps: Agree the reporting format and the forum (board, risk committee or executive meeting).
Report at least twice a year: programme status, open risks, incidents, requests, regulator contact.
Record decisions and track the actions they create.

NG.note: Forms part of the record verified at the annual audit.

EU.note: DPO reports to the highest management level.

controls.title: Programme resourcing and budget
controls.objective: The programme has the people, tools and budget its plan needs, agreed each year against the risk profile.
steps: Estimate effort from the tailored plan.
Decide what is done in-house and what is bought (DPO service, DPCO, tooling, training).
Approve the budget and record it.

controls.title: Accountability evidence index
controls.objective: For every control in the plan, you can produce the evidence within a day.
steps: Decide where evidence lives and how it is versioned.
Link each implemented control to its evidence.
Check the index before each audit or filing.
deliverables: Evidence index (this plan, with evidence links)
controls.notes: Tenet links records to controls automatically where it can. The index is this plan.

controls.title: Privacy objectives and key indicators
controls.objective: The programme has measurable objectives and a small set of indicators reviewed by management.
steps: Set three to five objectives for the year.
Choose indicators: request timeliness, DPIA coverage, vendor DPA coverage, training completion, incident notification timeliness.
Report them in the management report.
evidence: Indicator report over at least two periods

ISO27701: 6.2 Privacy objectives and planning to achieve them

controls.title: Applicable law and role analysis
controls.objective: For each entity you know which laws apply, whether you act as controller, processor or both, and which size or sector tiers you fall into.
steps: List where each entity is established and where its data subjects are.
Apply each law’s territorial test, including targeting tests for foreign entities.
Decide controller or processor role per main activity.
Work out size and sector tiers (for example the NDPA major-importance tiers).
evidence: Register with reasons for each conclusion

NG.ref: NDPA s.2; GAID 2025 Art. 8(2) (operating in Nigeria)

ISO27701: 4.1 Understanding the organisation and its context
4.2 Needs and expectations of interested parties

controls.title: Regulator registration, licences and fees
controls.objective: Every entity that must register, hold a licence or pay a fee has done so, and renewals are diarised.
steps: Check each law’s registration test and exemptions.
File registrations or licence applications with the required details.
Record numbers, expiry dates and renewal rules.
Set reminders well before expiry.

NG.ref: NDPA s.44; GAID 2025 (registration of data controllers and processors of major importance)
NG.note: Threshold and tier rules taken from practitioner summaries.

KE.ref: Kenya DPA s.18; Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations 2021

GH.ref: Act 843 (registration with the Data Protection Commission, renewable every two years)

EG.ref: PDPL 151/2020 and Executive Regulations 2025 (licences and permits from the PDPC)

ZW.ref: CDPA 2021; SI 155 of 2024 (data controller licence from POTRAZ)

UK.note: Annual data protection fee unless exempt.

controls.title: Statutory filings and returns calendar
controls.objective: Every recurring filing (audit returns, renewals, annual reports) is in one calendar with owners and lead times, and none is missed.
steps: List each filing, its trigger, deadline and who files it.
Work back from each deadline to the evidence needed.
Engage any licensed third party (such as a DPCO) early.
Record the filing and the regulator’s acknowledgement.

NG.ref: NDPA s.44; GAID 2025 (Compliance Audit Return through a licensed DPCO by 31 March)
NG.note: Fees apply from the 2026 cycle; late filing attracts a penalty. The 2025 return deadline was extended to 30 May 2026.

controls.title: Local representative
controls.objective: Where a law requires a representative because you are not established there, one is appointed in writing and named in your notices.
steps: Confirm the representative test applies and no exemption fits.
Appoint a representative by written mandate.
Name the representative in privacy notices and the record of processing.

controls.title: Legal and regulatory change watch
controls.objective: New laws, regulations, guidance and enforcement decisions are tracked, assessed for impact and turned into plan changes.
steps: Choose sources for each law in scope (regulator sites, gazettes, trusted alerts).
Log each change with an impact rating.
Turn material changes into tasks in this plan.

ISO27701: 4.1 Understanding the organisation and its context

controls.notes: Live items as at November 2026: the EU Digital Omnibus (Council position agreed, not law); Ghana’s Data Protection Bill 2025 (pending); Kenya’s Data Protection (Amendment) Bill (proposed); the NDPC’s DPO continuing professional development framework (June 2026).

controls.title: Regulator engagement and investigations
controls.objective: Regulator letters, audits and investigations are handled by a defined process, with deadlines met and privilege considered.
steps: Name who receives and who answers regulator correspondence.
Log each contact and its deadline.
Prepare an evidence pack from the accountability index.
Review the response with legal before sending.
evidence: Log of regulator contact and responses

controls.title: Prior authorisation and prior consultation
controls.objective: Processing that needs the regulator’s prior authorisation or consultation is identified before it starts and does not begin without it.
steps: Build the authorisation and consultation tests into DPIA screening.
Prepare submissions with the DPIA attached.
Hold the launch until the regulator responds or the statutory period ends.

ZA.note: Prior authorisation for listed processing such as unique identifiers linked across purposes and criminal or credit information.

KE.ref: Kenya DPA s.31 (DPIA submission to the Data Commissioner)

EG.ref: PDPL 151/2020 (permits for sensitive data and transfers)

controls.title: System and data asset inventory
controls.objective: Every system, SaaS tool, file store and paper record that holds personal data is listed with its owner, location and hosting country.
steps: Start from finance (software spend), IT asset lists and SSO logs.
Interview each department about what it uses, including spreadsheets and paper.
Record owner, hosting country, vendor and key security measures.
evidence: Inventory with owners and hosting locations

ISO27701: Annex A: inventory of information and assets

controls.title: Record of processing activities
controls.objective: Each processing activity is recorded with its purpose, lawful basis, data categories, data subjects, systems, recipients, transfers and retention, and the record is kept current.
steps: Run short workshops with each department, starting with HR, customers and marketing.
Record each activity against the inventory of systems.
Have each activity owner confirm their entries.
Review twice a year and whenever a DPIA or new vendor touches the activity.

NG.ref: GAID 2025 (record of processing activities, verified at audit)

EU.note: Exemption for fewer than 250 employees is narrow.

ISO27701: Annex A: records related to processing PII

controls.notes: The EU Digital Omnibus proposes lighter record-keeping for smaller organisations; it is not law. Keep the record regardless: the other laws in scope and the annual audit still rely on it.

controls.title: Records of processing carried out for clients
controls.objective: Where you act as processor, you keep a record of the processing you carry out for each client, with sub-processors and transfers.
steps: List clients for whom you process personal data and the services involved.
Record categories of processing, sub-processors, transfers and security measures per client.
Keep it aligned with the DPAs you have signed.

ISO27701: Annex A.2: records related to processing PII (processor)

controls.title: Data flow and transfer map
controls.objective: You can show how personal data moves between systems, vendors and countries for each main activity.
steps: Link activities to systems and vendors.
Record hosting and access countries.
Mark flows that cross borders and the basis relied on.

controls.title: Data classification scheme
controls.objective: Personal data is classified by sensitivity so that handling rules, access and security follow the class.
steps: Define three or four classes, with sensitive data under each law in scope at the top.
Set handling rules for each class.
Label systems and activities.

controls.title: Automated discovery of personal data
controls.objective: Structured and unstructured stores are scanned for personal data so that the inventory reflects reality, including shadow copies.
steps: Select discovery tooling that runs inside your environment and returns metadata only.
Scan the highest-risk stores first.
Reconcile findings against the inventory and record of processing.

controls.title: Lawful basis documented for each purpose
controls.objective: Every processing purpose has a lawful basis chosen before processing starts, justified in writing and valid under each law in scope.
steps: For each activity, choose the basis and record why it fits.
Check the basis exists under every law in scope; some laws lack legitimate interests or public task.
Avoid consent where there is an imbalance of power, such as employment.
deliverables: Lawful basis per activity in the record

UK.note: Recognised legitimate interests (Annex 1) available from 5 February 2026 under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

controls.title: Legitimate interests assessments
controls.objective: Each reliance on legitimate interests is supported by a purpose, necessity and balancing test that is recorded and reviewed.
steps: List activities relying on legitimate interests.
Complete the three-part test for each.
Record any safeguards, including an easy objection route.

NG.ref: NDPA s.25(1)(b)(v); GAID 2025 (legitimate interest assessments reviewed at audit)

controls.title: Consent capture, records and withdrawal
controls.objective: Where consent is relied on, it is specific, informed and unambiguous, is recorded with what the person saw, and is as easy to withdraw as to give.
steps: Inventory every consent request.
Fix wording, granularity and pre-ticked boxes.
Store consent records: who, when, what text, which channel.
Build withdrawal into each channel and propagate it to downstream systems.

ISO27701: Annex A.1: obtain and record consent

controls.title: Conditions for sensitive data
controls.objective: Each use of sensitive or special category data meets a specific condition under each law in scope, with the extra documentation some laws require.
steps: Identify activities using sensitive data under each law’s own list.
Record the condition relied on.
Write any required policy document (for example the UK appropriate policy document).
Apply stronger security and access limits.
deliverables: Sensitive data conditions in the record

UK.ref: UK GDPR Arts. 9–10; DPA 2018 Sch. 1 (appropriate policy document)

controls.notes: Lists differ: Kenya treats property, marital and family details as sensitive; Egypt includes financial data; POPIA includes criminal behaviour.

controls.title: Children’s data
controls.objective: Services likely to be used by children have age assurance proportionate to risk, parental consent where the law requires it, and child-appropriate design.
steps: Identify services and activities involving children.
Apply the age threshold and consent rule of each law in scope.
Design defaults for children: high privacy, no profiling for marketing, clear language.
deliverables: Age assurance and parental consent design

UK.ref: UK GDPR Art. 8; Age Appropriate Design Code
UK.note: The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 adds a duty to consider children’s higher protection matters for online services.

ISO27701: Annex A.1: obtain and record consent

controls.title: Purpose limitation and compatibility checks
controls.objective: New uses of existing data are checked for compatibility with the original purpose before they start.
steps: Add a compatibility question to change and project intake.
Record the assessment and any new basis or notice needed.

UK.note: The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 adds Annex 2 compatible purposes.

ISO27701: Annex A.1: identify and document purpose

controls.title: Direct marketing rules
controls.objective: Electronic and other direct marketing meets each law’s consent, soft opt-in and opt-out rules, and suppression lists are honoured everywhere.
steps: List marketing channels and the basis for each.
Fix consent and opt-out mechanics.
Maintain one suppression list used by every tool.

NG.note: Right to object, including to direct marketing.

UK.note: PECR fines raised to UK GDPR levels by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

controls.title: Privacy notices for customers and the public
controls.objective: Clear, layered notices tell people what you collect, why, on what basis, who receives it, where it goes, how long you keep it, their rights and how to complain.
steps: Draft from the record of processing, not from a template.
Include each law’s mandatory items and the regulator’s contact.
Publish where data is collected and keep versions.
evidence: Published notice with version and date

UK.note: From 19 June 2026 notices must also tell people about the right to complain to the controller.

ISO27701: Annex A.1: provide information to PII principals

controls.title: Employee and candidate privacy notices
controls.objective: Staff, contractors and applicants receive a notice covering HR processing, monitoring and their rights.
steps: Draft from the HR activities in the record.
Cover monitoring, background checks and retention.
Issue at onboarding and in the recruitment flow.

ISO27701: Annex A.1: provide information to PII principals

controls.title: Cookies and similar technologies
controls.objective: Non-essential cookies and trackers only run with valid consent where required, refusal is as easy as acceptance, and the cookie notice matches what is actually set.
steps: Scan sites and apps to list every cookie, SDK and pixel.
Classify each as essential, analytics, functional or advertising.
Configure consent before non-essential tags fire.
Re-scan after each release that changes tags.

EU.note: The Digital Omnibus would add consent-free purposes and single-click refusal; not law as at November 2026.

UK.note: Exemptions for certain analytics and functionality cookies in force from 5 February 2026.

controls.title: Access-to-information manual
controls.objective: The manual describing your records, processing and how to request access is current, published and filed where required.
steps: Update the manual from the record of processing.
Include the POPIA processing information.
Publish on the website and make it available at the head office.

controls.title: Monitoring and CCTV notices
controls.objective: People are told before they are monitored by CCTV, telematics, workplace monitoring or biometric systems, and monitoring is proportionate.
steps: List monitoring systems and their purposes.
Place signage and layered notices.
Set access and retention rules for footage and logs.

controls.title: Just-in-time notices and privacy dashboards
controls.objective: Products explain data use at the moment it matters and give people self-service controls over their data and preferences.
steps: Identify moments where people make data choices.
Add contextual explanations and controls.
Offer a preference centre that writes to the consent records.

controls.title: Rights request procedure
controls.objective: A written procedure covers every right available under each law in scope, with deadlines, extensions, exemptions and refusal grounds.
steps: List the rights and deadlines for each law in scope.
Set the verification standard and the search method.
Write templates for each response and refusal.

UK.note: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 rules on time limits and reasonable searches apply to requests from 5 February 2026.

ISO27701: Annex A.1: obligations to PII principals

controls.title: Request intake and identity verification
controls.objective: Requests are recognised on any channel, logged the same day, and identity is verified proportionately without asking for more data than needed.
steps: Train front-line staff to recognise requests in any wording.
Provide a web form and a monitored mailbox.
Apply the verification standard from the procedure.
evidence: Request log entries with receipt dates

ISO27701: Annex A.1: obligations to PII principals

controls.title: Request log and deadline tracking
controls.objective: Every request is logged with its deadline under the requester’s law and is answered on time.
steps: Log every request with type, law and deadline.
Track extensions and their notified reasons.
Review overdue items weekly.

controls.title: System search, extraction and erasure playbooks
controls.objective: For each system there is a tested way to find, export, correct and delete one person’s data.
steps: Write a short playbook per system: search keys, export, correction and deletion steps.
Test with a dummy record.
Include backups and vendor systems.

controls.title: Complaints handling
controls.objective: People can complain to you about how their data is handled, complaints are acknowledged and investigated, and they are told how to escalate to the regulator.
steps: Publish how to complain.
Acknowledge, investigate proportionately and keep the person informed.
Record each complaint, the steps taken and the outcome.
evidence: Log with acknowledgement and outcome dates

UK.ref: DPA 2018 ss.164A–164B (inserted by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025)
UK.note: In force 19 June 2026: acknowledge within 30 days, investigate without undue delay, keep records.

NG.ref: NDPA s.46; GAID 2025 (complaints and remediation reviewed at audit)

controls.title: Rights and complaints review
controls.objective: Trends in requests and complaints are reviewed so root causes are fixed rather than handled one case at a time.
steps: Report volumes, timeliness and outcomes.
Identify recurring causes.
Feed fixes into the plan.

controls.title: Privacy risk method and register
controls.objective: Privacy risks to individuals and to the organisation are assessed with one method and held in a register with owners and treatments.
steps: Adopt a likelihood and severity scale focused on harm to people.
Align it with the enterprise risk method.
Populate the register from the record of processing and recent incidents.
evidence: Register with owners and treatment dates

controls.title: DPIA screening at intake
controls.objective: New projects, systems, vendors and changes are screened for DPIA triggers under each law in scope before work starts.
steps: Add a screening question set to project, procurement and change intake.
Include each law’s trigger list.
Record screening outcomes, including decisions not to do a DPIA.

GH.note: The pending Data Protection Bill 2025 would make DPIAs mandatory for high-risk processing.

EU.note: National DPIA lists apply; the Digital Omnibus would replace them with one EU list (not law).

controls.title: DPIAs completed, signed off and reviewed
controls.objective: Required DPIAs are completed before processing, with DPO advice, risk treatment and sign-off, and reviewed when processing changes.
steps: Complete the DPIA with the project team.
Record DPO advice and the decision on it.
Track mitigations to completion.
Set a review date.

controls.title: Privacy by design in change and development
controls.objective: Privacy requirements are built into product, system and process design, with defaults that collect and expose the least data.
steps: Add privacy requirements to design templates and definitions of done.
Give engineers patterns: minimisation, pseudonymisation, retention hooks, access by role.
Review high-risk designs with the privacy lead.

ISO27701: Annex A.1: privacy by design and by default

controls.title: Risk treatment and acceptance
controls.objective: Risks above appetite are treated or formally accepted by the right person, and residual risk is tracked.
steps: Set a risk appetite and acceptance authority.
Track treatment actions to completion.
Record formal acceptance of residual risk.

controls.title: Privacy threat modelling
controls.objective: High-risk systems are threat-modelled for privacy (linkability, identifiability, disclosure, unawareness, non-compliance) as well as security.
steps: Choose a method such as LINDDUN.
Model the highest-risk systems first.
Track resulting design changes.

controls.title: Vendor and processor register
controls.objective: Every third party that receives or accesses personal data is listed with its role, service, location and contract status.
steps: Build the list from accounts payable and the system inventory.
Classify each as processor, sub-processor, joint or independent controller.
Record country and contract status.

ISO27701: Annex A.3: information security in supplier relationships

controls.title: Vendor due diligence before engagement
controls.objective: Processors are only engaged after checking they give sufficient guarantees, scaled to the data and risk involved, and the record of that check is kept.
steps: Tier vendors by data sensitivity, volume and location.
Use a questionnaire proportionate to the tier.
Review certifications, breach history and sub-processors.
Record the decision and any conditions.

NG.ref: GAID 2025 (due diligence on processors; records producible to the Commission)

ISO27701: Annex A.3: information security in supplier relationships

controls.title: Data processing agreements
controls.objective: Every processor relationship has a written agreement with the terms each law in scope requires.
steps: Prepare a DPA template that covers every law in scope.
Prioritise high-risk vendors.
Track signature and any negotiated deviations.

ISO27701: Annex A.1: contracts with PII processors

controls.title: Cross-border transfer mechanisms
controls.objective: Every transfer outside a jurisdiction rests on a valid mechanism under that jurisdiction’s law, recorded against the flow.
steps: List transfers from the flow map and vendor register.
Pick the mechanism per law: adequacy, approved clauses, binding corporate rules, or a derogation.
Put the mechanism in place and record it.

GH.ref: Data Protection Bill 2025 (pending): transfer rules and transfer impact assessments

UK.note: “Not materially lower” test in force from 5 February 2026.

controls.title: Transfer impact assessments
controls.objective: Transfers relying on contractual safeguards are assessed for the destination’s laws and practices, with supplementary measures where needed.
steps: Prioritise transfers of sensitive data and large volumes.
Assess destination access laws and practices.
Record supplementary measures and the conclusion.

EU.note: Expected under the EDPB’s recommendations on supplementary measures.

controls.title: Sub-processor oversight
controls.objective: You know each processor’s sub-processors, approve changes as your contracts require, and can object.
steps: Obtain sub-processor lists.
Subscribe to change notices.
Assess material changes.

ISO27701: Annex A.2: engagement of a subcontractor

controls.title: Periodic vendor review and exit
controls.objective: Vendors are re-reviewed on a cycle set by their risk tier, and data is returned or deleted with proof when a relationship ends.
steps: Set review cycles by tier.
Re-run due diligence at each review.
Obtain deletion or return certificates at exit.

controls.title: Data sharing and joint controller arrangements
controls.objective: Sharing with other controllers is documented, lawful and governed by an agreement setting each party’s responsibilities.
steps: List recurring sharing with other controllers.
Document the basis and conditions.
Sign data sharing or joint controller agreements.

UK.ref: UK GDPR Art. 26; ICO data sharing code

controls.title: Processor duties to clients
controls.objective: When you act as processor, you follow client instructions, help them meet their obligations, notify them of breaches without delay, and control your own sub-processors.
steps: Standardise your own DPA offered to clients.
Set up an internal route for client instructions and assistance requests.
Set breach notification to clients in hours, not days.

NG.note: Processor notifies the controller of a breach.

controls.title: Security policy and risk-based measures
controls.objective: An information security policy and baseline set measures appropriate to the risk of the personal data processed.
steps: Adopt a security policy and a baseline control set.
Map the baseline to the classification scheme.
Record gaps and treatments in the risk register.

ISO27701: Annex A.3: shared information security controls

controls.notes: If you hold or are building towards ISO/IEC 27001, reuse its policy and Statement of Applicability rather than writing a parallel set.

controls.title: Access control, least privilege and MFA
controls.objective: Access to personal data is granted by role, reviewed regularly and protected by multi-factor authentication on remote and privileged access.
steps: Define roles and what each may access.
Enforce MFA on email, remote access, admin and systems with sensitive data.
Review access quarterly for high-risk systems and at every leaver.

controls.title: Encryption in transit and at rest
controls.objective: Personal data is encrypted in transit everywhere and at rest wherever the classification requires it, with keys managed properly.
steps: Enforce TLS on all services.
Encrypt laptops, mobile devices, databases and backups holding sensitive data.
Document key management.
controls.notes: Encryption also matters for breach duties: several laws relax notification to individuals when data was unintelligible.

controls.title: Logging and monitoring of access to personal data
controls.objective: Access to systems holding personal data is logged, logs are protected, and unusual access is detected and investigated.
steps: Turn on access logging for high-risk systems.
Centralise and protect logs.
Set alerts for bulk export and out-of-hours access.

controls.title: Backup, resilience and restoration
controls.objective: Personal data can be restored in time after an incident, and restores are tested.
steps: Back up systems according to their criticality.
Protect backups from ransomware.
Test restores twice a year.

controls.title: Security testing and vulnerability management
controls.objective: Systems holding personal data are patched, scanned and tested, and the effectiveness of measures is evaluated regularly.
steps: Patch within defined timelines.
Scan for vulnerabilities monthly.
Commission a penetration test of internet-facing systems each year.

ISO27701: Annex A.3: management of technical vulnerabilities

controls.title: Endpoint, device and physical security
controls.objective: Laptops, phones, removable media, paper files and premises are protected in line with the data they hold.
steps: Manage devices centrally with encryption and remote wipe.
Set clear-desk and secure-print rules.
Control access to records rooms and data centres.

ISO27701: Annex A.3: physical and endpoint controls

controls.title: Pseudonymisation and privacy-enhancing technologies
controls.objective: Analytics, testing and AI work use pseudonymised, synthetic or aggregated data wherever the purpose allows.
steps: Identify uses that do not need direct identifiers.
Provide pseudonymisation and masking tools.
Ban production personal data in test environments without approval.

EU.note: The Digital Omnibus would clarify when pseudonymised data is not personal data for a recipient; not law.

controls.title: Retention schedule
controls.objective: Each category of records has a retention period with its reason, trigger and disposal method, and systems are set to follow it.
steps: Collect statutory retention periods (tax, employment, sector rules).
Set periods for each activity in the record.
Approve the schedule and assign owners for disposal.

controls.title: Secure deletion and disposal
controls.objective: Data past its retention period is deleted, anonymised or securely destroyed, including in backups and with vendors, and disposal is recorded.
steps: Automate deletion where systems allow.
Run scheduled purges where they do not.
Use certified destruction for paper and devices.
Record what was disposed of.

controls.title: Data minimisation reviews
controls.objective: Forms, systems and datasets collect and keep only what each purpose needs, checked periodically.
steps: Review collection forms against purposes.
Remove fields that are not needed.
Record the review.

controls.title: Data quality and accuracy
controls.objective: Personal data used for decisions is accurate and up to date, and people can correct it easily.
steps: Identify data used for decisions about people.
Add validation and refresh routines.
Link correction requests to source systems.

controls.title: Archiving, legal holds and research use
controls.objective: Archived data, legal holds and research or statistical uses are governed so they do not become indefinite retention.
steps: Define when data moves to archive and who can access it.
Issue and release legal holds formally.
Apply research safeguards such as pseudonymisation.

controls.title: Breach response plan and team
controls.objective: A tested plan names the response team, decision-makers, external advisers and each law’s notification test and clock.
steps: Set roles: incident lead, privacy lead, legal, communications, IT.
Write each law’s notification test, clock and form into the plan.
Pre-arrange forensic and legal support.

NG.note: 72 hours from awareness where there is a risk to rights and freedoms.

ZA.note: As soon as reasonably possible; reported through the Information Regulator’s e-portal since 2025.

KE.note: 72 hours where there is a real risk of harm.

EG.note: 72 hours to the PDPC; individuals within three working days.

EU.note: 72 hours. The Digital Omnibus would move to 96 hours for high-risk breaches only; not law.

ISO27701: Annex A.3: information security incident management

controls.title: Detection and internal reporting
controls.objective: Staff and vendors report suspected breaches immediately through a known channel, and the clock is started correctly.
steps: Publish one reporting channel.
Tell staff what to report and how fast.
Require vendors to report within hours.
evidence: Incident records with discovery and awareness times

ISO27701: Annex A.3: information security event reporting

controls.title: Breach assessment and regulator notification
controls.objective: Each incident is assessed against each affected law’s test, and regulators are notified on time with the required content, or the decision not to notify is recorded.
steps: Assess likelihood and severity of harm.
Apply each law’s test and start each clock.
Notify with the required content, then update as facts emerge.

ISO27701: Annex A.3: response to information security incidents

controls.title: Notifying affected people
controls.objective: Where the law requires it, affected people are told promptly in plain language what happened and what they can do.
steps: Prepare notice templates.
Decide channel and timing.
Set up a support line for larger incidents.

controls.title: Breach register
controls.objective: Every personal data breach is recorded, notifiable or not, with facts, effects, decisions and remedial action.
steps: Log every incident.
Record the notification decision and its reasons.
Close with root cause and lessons.

controls.title: Breach exercises and lessons learned
controls.objective: The plan is rehearsed at least once a year and improved after every significant incident or exercise.
steps: Run a tabletop exercise with a realistic scenario across several laws.
Record gaps and fix them.

controls.title: Privacy training for all staff
controls.objective: Everyone with access to personal data completes induction and annual refresher training, and completion is tracked.
steps: Build a short course on the policy, recognising requests and reporting breaches.
Make it part of onboarding.
Track completion; chase below 90 percent.

controls.title: Confidentiality and the employee lifecycle
controls.objective: Staff and contractors are bound to confidentiality, and joiner, mover and leaver steps protect personal data.
steps: Add confidentiality terms to contracts.
Link HR events to access changes.
Recover devices and data at exit.

controls.title: Role-based training for high-risk roles
controls.objective: Roles with elevated risk (HR, customer service, marketing, engineering, data science) get training specific to their work.
steps: Identify high-risk roles.
Build short role modules.
Track completion separately.

controls.title: Privacy lead competence and professional development
controls.objective: The privacy lead and team hold the credentials the law or regulator expects and keep them current.
steps: Check credential requirements in each jurisdiction.
Plan certification and continuing education.
Keep evidence on file.

NG.ref: GAID 2025 (DPO credentials); NDPC CPD framework for certified DPOs (June 2026)

ZW.ref: SI 155 of 2024 (DPO certification course approved by the authority)

controls.title: Awareness and culture
controls.objective: Privacy is visible beyond annual training through campaigns, champion activity and leadership messages, and culture is measured.
steps: Plan a quarterly awareness calendar.
Use incidents and requests as teaching material.
Survey awareness once a year.

controls.title: AI system inventory
controls.objective: Every AI system and generative AI tool in use or development is listed with its purpose, owner, data, vendor and decision role.
steps: Survey teams and procurement for AI use, including free generative tools.
Record each system with its data and decision role.
Link systems to processing activities.

EU.note: Applies to deployers of high-risk systems in the EU.

ISO42001: 6.1 Actions to address risks and opportunities
Annex A: AI system inventory and resources

controls.title: AI acceptable use policy
controls.objective: Staff know which AI tools they may use, with what data, and what needs approval.
steps: List approved tools and prohibited data types.
Set an approval route for new tools.
Train staff on it.

controls.title: AI risk classification and impact assessment
controls.objective: Each AI system is classified against the laws in scope and assessed for impact on people before deployment.
steps: Classify each system (prohibited, high risk, limited, minimal; and data protection risk).
Extend the DPIA with model purpose, affected groups, bias and oversight.
Sign off before production.

EU.ref: EU AI Act Arts. 6, 27; GDPR Art. 35
EU.note: Fundamental rights impact assessment for listed deployers.

controls.title: Automated decisions: safeguards and human review
controls.objective: Decisions with legal or similarly significant effects made solely by automated means have a lawful basis, are explained, and can be contested before a human.
steps: Identify solely automated decisions with significant effects.
Confirm the basis and safeguards each law requires.
Provide explanation, a contest route and human review.

UK.note: Inserted by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; in force from 5 February 2026.

ISO42001: Annex A: use of AI systems; information for interested parties

controls.title: Training and input data governance
controls.objective: Personal data used to train, fine-tune or prompt AI systems has a lawful basis, is minimised and is recorded.
steps: Record data sources for each model.
Confirm basis and notice coverage for training use.
Minimise and pseudonymise before training.

EU.ref: GDPR Arts. 5, 6; EU AI Act Art. 10
EU.note: The Digital Omnibus Council text would confirm legitimate interests may support AI development, case by case; not law.

ISO42001: Annex A: data for AI systems

controls.title: AI vendor and model provider due diligence
controls.objective: AI vendors are assessed for training on customer data, retention, location, security and model documentation before use.
steps: Add AI questions to vendor due diligence.
Contract against training on your data where needed.
Record model cards or equivalent documentation.

ISO42001: Annex A: third-party and customer relationships

controls.title: AI monitoring, validation and bias testing
controls.objective: AI systems affecting people are validated before release and monitored for accuracy, drift and unfair outcomes.
steps: Define validation metrics including fairness across groups.
Monitor in production.
Re-validate after material changes.

EU.note: Mandatory for high-risk systems: providers test and monitor; deployers monitor operation.

ISO42001: Annex A: AI system life cycle

controls.title: Control self-assessment
controls.objective: Control owners confirm twice a year that their controls operate, with evidence, and gaps feed the plan.
steps: Send owners their controls and evidence requirements.
Review responses and sample evidence.
Raise gaps as tasks.

controls.title: Internal audit of the programme
controls.objective: An independent internal audit tests the programme against this framework and the laws in scope on a planned cycle.
steps: Plan audits by risk.
Audit with someone independent of the controls.
Report findings to management and track them.

controls.title: Management review
controls.objective: Top management reviews the programme at planned intervals and decides on changes, resources and improvement.
steps: Prepare inputs: audit results, indicators, incidents, regulatory changes.
Hold the review.
Record decisions and actions.

controls.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
controls.objective: Findings from audits, incidents, complaints and regulators are corrected at the root cause and checked for effectiveness.
steps: Log each finding.
Analyse root cause.
Track corrective action to verified closure.

controls.title: External audit readiness
controls.objective: The organisation can pass an external audit or regulator inspection without a scramble, with evidence current for every control.
steps: Run a mock audit against the regulator’s checklist.
Close gaps before the audit window.
Brief the people who will be interviewed.

NG.ref: GAID 2025 (annual audit by a licensed DPCO for upper-tier controllers)

KE.ref: ODPC compliance audits (draft Conduct of Compliance Audit regulations)

controls.title: Continual improvement and benchmarking
controls.objective: The programme measures its maturity each year, benchmarks itself, and sets the next year’s plan from the results.
steps: Score maturity by domain.
Compare with peers where data allows.
Set targets and update the plan.

controls.title: Certification
controls.objective: The privacy information management system is certified by an accredited body and the certificate is maintained.
steps: Define the certification scope.
Produce the Statement of Applicability against Annex A.
Complete stage 1 and stage 2 audits.
Plan surveillance audits.
controls.notes: ISO/IEC 27701:2025 can be certified on its own. Holders of 2019 certificates must transition by October 2028.
